Does our reverence for the old masters show that art needs more than a clever idea? Or will the test of time count unmade beds and formaldehyde sharks as equal with the Sistine Chapel?

title: The Self and the Selfie
description: With more data stored from one day's selfies than all the world's books, many have dismissed Generation Selfie as superficial and vain. Yet creative genius has often been linked to narcissism - Dali once quipped there was no greater joy than waking up as himself. Could focusing on ourselves rather than others be a route to happiness and success? Or is an obsession with ourselves damaging to social cohesion and a likely route to personal misery?

title: Global Overhaul
description: Philosopher and Green Party politician Rupert Read explores our moral obligations to the planet.

title: Decoding the Universe
description: Is information fundamental to the universe? Is reality no more than a strange string of code? Oxford University constructor theorist Chiara Marletto outlines a new theory which seeks to explain life, the universe and everything in it.

title: Securing Our Future
description: From LHC black holes to wars against robots, humanity faces new risks that are improbable but catastrophic. Oxford futurist Anders Sandberg outlines how we can save ourselves.

title: Seeing Through Psychosis
description: What can we learn from the experiences of psychosis? Actor and Comedian Juliette Burton uses her experience of mental illness to explore the strange world we're in.

title: The future of the post-truth world
description: Many are fearful as we rush headlong into a post-truth world. Post-truth may have begun as an attack on the lies and deceit of politicians, but it has now become the description of our age. The digital revolution was supposed to herald a new era of openness. Instead it has uncovered a myriad of contradictory perspectives and untrustworthy 'truths' where the loudest and most powerful threaten to be the only winners. So what is the truth about the world? Do we have to accept that, along with the liberal consensus, the era of objective truth is over? Or is there a way to row back from the chaos? And if post-truth is unavoidable, how should we make sense of the world, and more importantly, how might we make it a better place?

title: Return to Radical Feminism
description: Has contemporary feminism lost its way? London Feminist Network founder Finn Mackay brings 70s radicalism into the 21st century.

title: Duchamp's Deception
description: Duchamp’s infamous urinal gave birth to modern art as we know it. But was its founding father a fraud? Outspoken author and critic Julian Spalding uncovers a scandal.

title: Doctors in the Age of Google
description: Most of us still think doctor knows best. Yet a third of all hospital beds are filled with conditions caused by medical intervention. With sophisticated diagnosis just a web search away is it time to rid ourselves of medical authority? Or do we need doctors more than ever in the chaos of information?

title: Corruption and Climate Change
description: Is science more sinister than an honest pursuit of the truth? Outspoken astrophysicist Piers Corbyn reveals the hidden power structures that threaten our future in our free online video debate.

title: Dangerous Convictions
description: Nietzsche warned certainty leads to madness. Yet we still demand it of ourselves and others. Sociologist and author of Culture of Fear Frank Furedi asks: could we live without it?

title: Democracy and the Digital Revolution
description: Why have we let the internet disrupt the human experience? Corbyn's Shadow Minister for digital government and cyber security Chi Onwurah calls for a democratic revolution.

title: The Emperor's New Art
description: From the masks and jewellery of the Pharaohs to contemporary painting, art has always been valued above almost all else. Yet it has no practical purpose. Has money chased art because, with no objective measure, art is victim to limitless hype and fashion, or are gold baubles and diamond skulls of genuinely great value?

title: Life in the Universe
description: What does the hunt for extra-terrestrial life say about human nature? What will happen if the radio silence stops? Theologian, astrophysicist and author of God, Time & Stephen Hawking David Wilkinson explores.

title: What should we do about poverty?
description: Is government policy exacerbating poverty? Big Issue founder John Bird takes the government to task as he discusses his new political manifesto. "Eccentric, extraordinary but worldly wise" Polly Toynbee

title: In Search of Safety
description: Visions of a violent and lawless future are a commonplace, yet strangely crime has fallen 66% in the UK in the last two decades and we are less likely to fall victim to an act of violence than we have ever been. Do we want to imagine the world is dangerous because our lives have become too safe? Or is the world scarier than the figures suggest?

title: Democracy and Drugs
description: David Nutt was fired by the Home Secretary for comparing the harms of ecstasy and horse-riding. Hear his case for an evidence-based approach to drug policy and resurrecting the use of psychedelics as a treatment for mental illness.

title: The Death Drive
description: car crash; celebrity; celebrity culture; car; top gear; the grand tour; famous car crashes; car accident; car crash as cultural phenomenon; analysis of car crashes; car crash statistics;

title: In the Beginning Was the Word
description: In the 20th century we came to see language as radically more important than a mere vehicle for ideas. It was the framework that made thought possible.  But do animals not think? And can't humans think outside of language - knowing the way home for example? Is language not so central after all or is there really nothing outside of the text?

title: The New Bodies
description: Society now accepts gender and sexuality as fluid. Is the fluidity of the human body the next step forward? Bionic hand user and transhumanist Nicky Ashwell envisions the future.

title: Love Is the Drug
description: We’re happy taking drugs to fight depression. But what about a pill for engineering romance? Oxford neuroscientist and Future of Humanity Institute fellow Anders Sandberg makes the case for chemically enhancing our love lives.

title: Culture Shock
description: We think culture is always evolving. Yet from the death of subculture to our obsession with everything old-school, we seem in a strange cultural lull. Where are our punks, our Picassos and our Freuds? Has our culture run out of ideas, or are the great ideas and movements for our time already with us or just round the corner?

title: Radical Spirituality
description: Does the threat of Earth's destruction call for a profound change to how we see it? Environmentalist and author of Spiritual Activism Alastair McIntosh explains how to save the planet.

title: Sex and Love in the Digital Age
description: Is technology harming our relationships?

title: What happens to our bodies when we die?
description: What happens to our bodies when we die? Forensic scientist and Belle de Jour blogger Brook Magnanti anticipates life's strangest certainty. "A media sensation" Telegraph

title: After the End of Evidence
description: Has modern physics outgrown the need for evidence? New York philosopher Massimo Pigliucci argues for a new age of explanation.

title: Stories to Change the World
description: Free video debate: Literary theorist Stanley Fish, Entrepreneur Margaret Heffernan and Philosopher Stephen Neale explore the deeper properties of rhetoric

title: The Secret Conjurer
description: From the illusion of choice to the sensation of touch, the mind is a master of deception. Neuroscientist and author Susana Martinez-Conde unveils how to beat the brain at its own game.

title: Diversity and Difference
description: Disillusioned with the mainstream, Sophie Walker joined and now leads the Women's Equality Party. Here she asks: is radical thinking enough to change society?

title: What Machines Can't Do
description: From Alan Turing to Stephen Hawking, many claim computers could overtake humanity. But no computer can match human intelligence at the moment. So where is the limit between what computers, or robots, can and cannot actually do? When might machines match their makers? Or is this idea just a hype caused by a misunderstanding of what artificial intelligence is?

title: Mind and the Universe
description: The Science Delusion author Rupert Sheldrake strikes out against the orthodoxy and asks: is the sun conscious?

title: Cosmic Dreams
description: Over 40 years have passed since string theory was first developed: what questions have been answered? Philosopher James Ladyman examines one of our strangest endeavours.

title: Humans versus Nature
description: From the call of the mountains to the preservation of wilderness, we wish to celebrate and protect nature as something precious.  But what separates humanity and its actions from nature remains a mystery. Are humans a malevolent force destroying the purity of the natural world? Or are we part of nature ourselves and necessarily at one with it? Explorer Bruce Parry, Green Party politician and philosopher Rupert Read, and author of What is Nature? Kate Soper debate our place in the world.

title: Could sex robots be good for us?
description: As the robots of the future march into the present, what are the ethical implications for relationships between man and machine? Computer scientist and artificial sexuality expert Kate Devlin considers a future taboo.

title: Doctors and the Danger Industry
description:
For the first time in a century, today's treatments may be less effective than before. 
Outspoken Psychiatrist David Healy reveals the market forces that threaten our health.

title: The strangeness of things
description: Free Video Debate: CERN physicist John Ellis, philosopher Hilary Lawson and film-maker David Malone go in search of the ultimate nature of things.

title: Free Thought
description: Free Video Talk: Are universities threatening free speech? Author and human rights activist Peter Tatchell speaks out against censorship.

title: Gravity minus dark matter
description: Philosophy & Science Video: Do dark energy and dark matter hint at an uncovered reality? Physicist Erik Verlinde outlines his theory where spacetime and gravity dissolve.

title: Knowing Others and Knowing Oneself
description: Philosophy Video Debate: Watch Robert Eaglestone, Nick Humphrey and Anita Avramides discuss if we have unique knowledge of our own mind and hiow we can get to understand the minds of others.

title: On Evil
description: Why does the strange nature of evil still hold us captive in our secular age? Danish author of Nothing Janne Teller reveals what lies behind our darkest fascinations.

title: Hearts and Minds
description: Free Video Lecture by the Institute of Art and Ideas - Watch Oxford philosopher Peter Hacker setting out his unique theory of the emotions.

title: After The Crisis
description:
Are China's downturn and uncertainty in the Eurozone tremors of an upcoming crisis or are we still recovering from the crash?

"The Stephen Hawking of economics" (Guardian) Anatole Kaletsky examines 2016's instability.

title: On the Air with Annie Nightingale
description: The first female to enter the RA Hall of Fame, MBE recipient Annie Nightingale is the BBC's longest serving DJ. Join the "first lady of radio" as she discusses 50 years at the forefront of Britain's shifting music scene.

title: The Story of Romance
description: From love at first sight to falling head over heels, it seems love isn’t something we do but something that happens to us. Yet relationship experts say successful relationships are built on hard work. Can we construct the romantic narrative? Would power over love’s story improve the experience? Or is love a wild adventure left best untamed?

title: Quantum Whispers
description: Is teleportation no longer confirmed to fiction? Physicist and quantum communications pioneer Lev Vaidman reports on the field’s current progress and asks: what do the laws of nature allow?

title: The Shame Game
description: Comedian Robin Ince, author Helen Croydon, and theologian and Zizek collaborator John Milbank uncover the strangeness of shame, and ask if it's a tool for change or a tyranny of the mob.

title: Politics and the Patriarchy
description: Has Westminster really made progress to equality? Former Primeminister David Cameron told Shadow Secretary for Business Angela Eagle to “Calm down, dear”; here she forecasts the future of sexism in politics.

title: Who We Have Been and Who We Are
description: Journalist Yasmin Alibhai Brown, author of Doctoring the Mind Richard Bentall, and post-modern sociologist Steve Fuller hold memory to account.

title: The Sound of the Self
description: King's College London New Thinkers: how do sonic experiences in literature define us? Emilie Gautier reveals what Thomas Hardy's world discloses.

title: A Fairytale Romance
description: Screw the Fairytale author Helen Croydon, UCL anthropologist Kit Opie, and psychologist Susan Quilliam imagine new models for relationships.

title: What We Cannot Know
description: The headlines of new discoveries about the universe continue, but are we approaching our limits? Mathematician and broadcaster Marcus du Sautoy explores.

title: Language and the World
description: American philosopher Nancy Cartwright, closure theorist Hilary Lawson and Director of the Centre for Logic and Language Corine Besson debate the limits of language.

title: Lies and beauty
description: New York philosopher and author of Lying for the Sake of Truth James Mahon, Absolutely Fabulous star Helen Lederer, and psychiatrist Mark Salter dissect the ethics of deceit.

title: The Swindle of the New
description: In our topsy-turvy postmodern world, we're held captive by the promise of the new. One of Britain's most influential cultural critics Terry Eagleton examines novelty's strange perils.

title: Generation Rent: Sharing the Future
description: Guardian columnist Zoe Williams, architecture critic and author of A New Kind of Bleak Owen Hatherley, and commentator Simon Heffer investigate the housing crisis.

title: The Beautiful Universe
description: Author of Aesthetics and Subjectivity: from Kant to Nietzsche Andrew Bowie, philosopher Joanna Burch-Brown and Young British Artist Gavin Turk look for beauty in the world.

title: Broken Beauty
description: How can art survive the onslaught of oil and money? Artist and activist Mel Evans explores the dark relationships between art, oil and the market.

title: Beware Bankers Bearing Gifts
description: Capitalism 4.0 author Anatole Kaletsky, Senior Economic Adviser at HSBC Stephen King and LSE anthropologist Laura Bear dispute morality and money.

title: Diversity and Power
description: Disillusioned with the mainstream, Sophie Walker joined and now leads the Women's Equality Party. Here she asks: is radical thinking enough to change society?

title: Love me Tinder
description:
KCL philosopher Christopher Hamilton, eHarmony’s Chief Scientist Steve
Carter, and Oxford neuroscientist Anders Sandberg tackle technology’s
impact on our relationships.

title: Philosophy in the bedroom
description: For 250 years de Sade's writing was outlawed. Yet Fifty Shades has turned the exploration of pain and pleasure into an oddly commonplace entertainment. Are these pursuits essential to our sexuality?

title: Blind Data
description: eHarmony's Chief Scientist Steve Carter unveils new research into the science of love and compatibility.

title: The Vital Statistics
description: Darwinian philosopher Helena Cronin argues that gender differences should be accepted not ignored.

title: Conditions for creativity
description:
Author and former model Jenny Boyd, British pop artist Allen Jones and
transhumanist and futurist Anders Sandberg test the limits of creativity.

title: Beyond experience
description: CERN physicist Tara Shears, author of Closure and post-postmodern metaphysician Hilary Lawson, and theologian Alison Milbank question reality beyond experience.

title: The Chemistry of Desire
description: Belle de Jour blogger Brooke Magnanti, Cambridge evolutionary psychologist Nicholas Humphrey and journalist and author of The Game Neil Strauss pursue true romance.

title: After Buddhism
description: What could secular Buddhist philosophy bring to a dissatisfied West? Buddhist teacher and author Stephen Batchelor gives ancient wisdom a 21st century home.

title: Gravity
description: Theoretical physicist Laura Mersini-Houghton, Nobel Prize-winner Frank Wilczek and string theorist Eric Verlinde examine the enigma of gravity.

title: The good, the bad, and the unknown
description: Centre for Secular Space founder Gita Sahgal, philosopher and author of Causes and Coincidences David Owens, and director of the Centre for Effective Altruism Sebastian Farquhar discuss the outcomes of our actions.

title: Not Only Rock 'n' Roll
description: From flower power in New York to sitting on ashram roofs with the Beatles, model turned psychologist Jenny Boyd reveals what it was like at the fore of the 60s cultural revolution.

title: A Politics of Hope
description:
Where are the alternatives to injustice and uncertainty? Author of The Establishment Owen Jones makes the case for an end to despair and a new era of politics.
 “Our generation’s Orwell” Russell Brand

title: In search of ourselves
description: Philosopher and author of The Singularity David Chalmers joins explorer Ed Stafford and award-winning novelist Joanna Kavenna to discover what lies within.

title: Space Hacks
description: Space security expert and Chatham House Research Director Patricia Lewis reveals the silent dangers in space.

title: Emperor's New Genes
description: Author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake, Imperial College geneticist Anne Bowcock, and author of The Music of Life Denis Noble look beyond the genome.

title: Life On The Edge
description: How can we rethink society to halt existential crises as rapidly as threats can occur? Director of the Centre for Effective Altruism Sebastian Farquhar outlines his solution.

title: The Limits of Freedom
description: Freedom is a goal we all endorse. Yet as neuroscience shows and history suggests, we are less content when we have more choice. Is too much freedom paradoxically debilitating? Do we need constraints to thrive, and might our chains and limitations be key to our freedom? Or is this a dangerous conceit of the privileged and free? Psychiatrist Theodore Dalrymple, Blair's former Senior Policy Advisor Julian Le Grand and author of I Find That Offensive Claire Fox interrogate choice.

title: After the Higgs Boson
description: In 2013 we found the Higgs boson. Then, earlier this year, we found Gravitational Waves. Eminent CERN physicist John Ellis asks: what's next for 21st century physics?

title: The illusion of sense
description: Cognitive neuroscientist Ophelia Deroy, philosopher and author of Philosophy for Life Rupert Read, and closure theorist Hilary Lawson confront the limits of perception.

title: A Tribal World
description: Author of Exotic England Yasmin Alibhai-Brown, editor of Spiked Brendan O'Neill, journalist Julie Bindel and director of the Forum for European Philosophy Simon Glendinning seek the truth about the tribe.

title: Love Story
description: 'Screw the Fairytale' author Helen Croydon joins Ethicist Naomi Goulder and transhumanist Anders Sandberg to rethink romance.

title: Madness and wisdom
description: Author of Madness Explained Richard Bentall, psychiatrist Patricia Casey and philosopher and author of Death Drive Robert-Rowland Smith dispute meaning and madness.

title: The Known, The Strange and the New
description: Eminent CERN physicist John Ellis joins Robert Rowland-Smith and existential novelist of Nothing Janne Teller to confront the strangeness of reality.

title: Dreaming the Future
description: Philosopher and author Roger Scruton, Green Party Leader Natalie Bennett and MP and ResPublica Director Phillip Blond confront the future

title: Sisters and the Sisterhood
description: American civil rights advocate Kimberle Crenshaw, joins Wilful Blindness author Margaret Heffernan and outspoken journalist Myriam Francois.

title: Owning Ourselves
description: Belle de Jour blogger Brooke Magnanti, bioethicist John Harris, and author of Our Bodies, Whose Property? Anne Phillips interrogate ownership.

description: Author of Time Reborn Lee Smolin, live from Ontario, joins theoretical physicist Michael Duff and KCL metaphysician Eleanor Knox to reunite science and experience.

title: Equality and Difference
description: Former Green Party Leader Natalie Bennett, ResPublica director Phillip Blond, and Unilever's Social Impact Vice President Marcela Manubens examine equality.

title: The Good, The Bad, and the Controversial
description: Spiked Online Editor Brendan Oneill joins NCH philosopher Naomi Goulder, journalist Sameer Rahim, and Coco de Mer founder Sam Roddick to seek answers.

description: Philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, CERN physicist Tara Shears and author of The Science Delusion Rupert Sheldrake ask if theories need evidence.

description: Civil Rights activist Kimberlé Crenshaw, journalist Juliet Jacques and philosopher Robert Eaglestone investigate the shared nature of emotion.

description: Biologist and author of Secret Life of Trees Colin Tudge, philosopher Rebecca Roache and science fiction author Richard Morgan debate discontent.

description: Philosopher and author of Western Philosophy John Cottingham, East End psychiatrist Mark Salter and science fiction and fantasy author Richard Morgan seek out the all-seeing I.

description: Zero Degrees of Empathy author Simon Baron-Cohen, philosopher Peter Dews and Oxford Transhumanist Anders Sadnberg dispute how to be good.

description: Star of Under the Skin Adam Pearson and author of How to Be Free Tom Hodgkinson are joined by UK editor of Broadly Zing Tseng to question the seduction of success.

description: Oxford constructor theorist Chiara Marletto, mathematician Peter Cameron, and string theorist Mike Duff untangle cause and effect.

description: Senior economic advisor at HSBC, Stephen King, author of Bouargeois Dignity Deirdre McClosky and cofounder of Novara Media Aaron Bastani take anarchy seriously.

description: Priest Rosie Harper, Oxford Chemist Peter Atkins, and philosopher of science Steve Fuller debate paradigms and power

title: Victims and conquerors
description: Niki Adams of the English Collective of Prostitutes joins commentator and author of Life at the Bottom Theodore Darlymple, and Catherine Hakim to examine one of society's last taboos.

title: The People's Champion
description: Author of The Establishment Owen Jones, ResPublica director and author of Radical Republic Phillip Blond, and conservative politician Charlotte Leslie examine the strange perils of democracy.

title: Avoiding Apocalypse
description: Nuclear Physicist Patritia Lewis, author of The Politics of Fear Frank Furedi and Green Party leader Natalie Bennett take the apocalypse seriously.

title: The puzzle of progress
description: Barry C. Smith asks philosopher and author of Middle Age Christopher Hamilton, digital editor of Newsweek Serena Kutchinsky and exlporer Bruce Parry how far we have come.

title: Romancing Opiates
description: What is the strange allure of opiate addiction? Author and former prison psychiatrist Thoeodre Dalrymple argues his personal take on the problems poppies pose.

title: A Philosophy of Confidence
description: Nietzsche famously said 'That which does not kill us makes us stronger', but how should we deal with failure? Author and Wired editor Rowland declares war on defeat.

description: Former chief speechwriter to Tony Blair Philip Collins and military historian Hew Strachan clash over the prospect of peace with founder of the Stop The War Coalition Lindsey German.

title: Brave New Horizon
description: Science fiction author Richard Morgan, first UK user of a bionic arm Nicky Ashwell and Oxford Fellow Anders Sandberg  debate the future of humanity.

title: A Goldilocks World
description: New York philosopher Massimo Pigliucci, M-Theorist and author of Universe or Multiverse? Bernard Carr, and Oxford constructor theorist Chiara Marletto wonder why we are here.

title: Forbidden Fantasies
description: Where should we draw the line on sexual fantasy? Former Erotic Review 'Editrice' Rowan Pelling ponders the intimate ideas banned from the bedroom.

title: Truth, Lies and Self-Deception
description: President of the Royal College of Psychiatry Simon Wessely, author of Nothing Janne Teller, and UCL neuroscientist Parashkev Nachev seek answers.

title: The Storm and the Butterfly
description: Philosopher and politician Rupert Read, eminent economist Anatole Kaletsky and lecturer Felix Reed-Tsochas find the edge of uncertainty.

title: Rethinking Feminism
description: We think feminism fights for equality for everyone. But from the right to wear headscarves to the refusal of contraception, ideas of what is fair and what equality is vary dramatically. Does feminism lack a universal goal because its an impossible dream? Must we recognise feminism means different things in different places or should we all fight for the same thing?

description: Anthropologist and author of Blue Jeans Daniel Miller, journalist and broadcaster Helen Croydon and former Harper's Bazaar editor and cultural commentator Peter York put fashion on trial.

description:
Tony Blair's former speechwriter Philip Collins dissects the results of the most anticipated election in a generation. 

"He has a talent for saying things people don't want to hear" Nick Pearce

description: Neurobiologist Steven Rose, President of the Royal College of Psychiatrists Sue Bailey and biographer Hermione Lee celebrate forgetfulness.

title: The Tyranny of Freedom
description: Renowned Slovenian philosopher Renata Salecl, feminist psychologist Lynne Segal and best-selling Candian philosopher Lou Marinoff question the limits of freedom.

title: Is Beauty Back?
description: Cortauld scholar and High Art Lite author Julian Stallabrass, eminent art historian Griselda Pollock and Norwegian artist Sidsel Christensen contemplate the new beautiful.

title: Uncovering Reality
description: Cambridge Professor of Applied Mathematics David Tong, quantum physicist Lev Vaidman and post-postmodern philosopher Hilary Lawson challenge the foundations of reality.

title: Are Selves Unreal?
description:
From Hume to Dennett, philosophers often claim that the self is an illusion, and neuroscientists and psychologists are inclined to agree. But are they wrong?

Moral philosopher and "The UK's foremost scourge of scientific pretension" Mary Midgley (Guardian) debunks the establishment's attack on the self.

title: Why It Is Hard to Imagine Anyone Winning the Next Election
description: Blair's former chief speechwriter looks to the future to find some unlikely partnerships.

title: How to Find a Multiverse
description: Laura Mersini-Houghton, multiverse theorist and UNC theoretical physicist, on how the latest snapshots from the Planck satellite yield evidence for parallel universes.
filename: HTLGI2013_318 How to find a multiverse.mp4

title: Why Some Politicians Are More Dangerous Than Others
description: Drawing on a century of evidence, American psychiatrist James Gilligan's theory has implications for every country that calls itself democratic and humane.

title: The immortal now
description: Neuroscientist Parashkev Nachev, polar guide and explorer Pen Hadow, and philosopher and author of Illness Havi Carel reason with the reaper.

title: At the world's edge
description: Philosopher Terry Eagleton and eminent novelist AS Byatt join Terry Pratchett to explore reality’s edge.

title: This Extraordinary World
description: In a culture besotted with glamour, the everyday can often seem banal. Michael Foley, author of Embracing the Ordinary and The Age of Absurdity, calls for us to see the world with fresh eyes.

title: Capitalism and the Common Good
description:
Has capitalism ceased to serve mankind? Baroness Williams seeks out meaningful change.

"A force to be reckoned with" Spectator

title: The Never-Ending Journey
description: The nomad is often seen as a romantic relic of a vanished way of life. But is this a fundamental misconception? Should we seek to protect and extend the possibility of a nomadic lifestyle, and place it at the heart of our culture? Or is the intellectual nomad a mascot of disarray and confusion?

title: Why there is something rather than nothing
video_url: https://iai.tv/assets/videos/linked/HTLGI2013_392 Why is there something rather than nothing.mp4
description: Why is there something instead of nothing? Laurence Krauss, John Ellis and Don Culpitt on the universe's orgins
filename: HTLGI2013_392 Why is there something rather than nothing.mp4

title: The Sexualisation of Society
description: Shadow Health Secretary Diane Abbott launches an assault on the hypersexualised culture of the UK and its damaging effect on youth.

title: The Next Fifty Years
description: Is Britain at a turning point as significant as Thatcher's victory in 1979? Former Mayor of London Ken Livingstone presents a new paradigm for British politics.

title: The Old Lady's Crisis
description: Capitalism 4.0 author Anatole Kaletsky, HBSC Chief Economist Stephen D. King and philosopher Jamie Whyte debate the Old Lady's monopoly.

title: More Than Equal
description: Director of think tank Demos David Goodhart, Respect MP George Galloway, and advocate and campaigner Peter Tatchell look beyond identity politics.

title: The Fragility of the Human Personality
description: Without possessions, what can be said to remain of 'us'? Christopher Hamilton reflects on Primo Levi and the idea of the self.

title: Death and the Human Animal
description: Mary Midgely - the “scourge of scientific pretention” (Guardian) - whose six-decade dominance of British philosophy has included Beast and Man and The Solitary Self.

title: Truth, Error & Adventure
description: Philosophers have placed truth at the centre of their account of meaning. But might this be a mistake? A radical reappraisal of the importance of error.

title: The Origin of Everything
description: What can science tell us about nothingness? From the origins of the universe to the limits of knowledge and the real differences between philosophy and science

title: Vive la Revolution
description: What do the principles of the French revolution mean to us today? Do liberty, equality, fraternity still have a guiding role to play in European politics?

title: How to Thrive in a Digital Age
description: We text, tweet & blog our way through life. What effect is constant connection really having? Tom Chatfield offers advice on how to prosper in a digital century

title: Hitler's Art War
description: Many people know that Hitler was a painter, but few know about his passion for collecting art, a passion so great that it could make a man go to war.

title: Poetic Theories
description: Can poetry contribute to the progress of science – as Richard Dawkins argues – or is the poet's eye & mind no more than an imaginative flourish?

title: Don Cupitt on Progress
description: Has technological advancement replaced moral, spiritual & political progress? Don Cupitt reflects on Nietzsche, the first world war and the way we live now

title: Mandela: Icon of Icons?
description: Drawing on 30 years as a campaigner against apartheid, Peter Hain examines the life & leadership of Nelson Mandela: a hero, a symbol… the icon of icons

title: The limits of science
description: Can science uncover the nature of the world? From the limits of science, boundaries of knowledge and philosophy, are we attracted by the universe’s mysteries?

title: Is digital thinking different?
description: The internet revolution is rewiring the human brain and society altogether. Is it the beginnings of a new digital intellectual culture or the dawn of a dark age?

title: Treating Psychosis
description: Clinical psychologist Richard Bentall presents new evidence for the limitations of anti-psychotic medication and of the psychiatric establishment

title: Con Art
description: From his book "Con Art: Why You Ought to Sell Your Damien Hirsts While You Can", Julian Spalding redefines the notion of conceptual art for the 21st century

title: Dangerous Dynasties and Blood Ties
description: From the Murdochs to the monarchy, blood ties permeate our meritocratic society. Is nepotism the natural order of things essential for a cohesive culture?

title: Life story
description: We all create internal narratives of our lives. Do these stories of ourselves simply reflect our lives, or do they determine who we are and what we can achieve?

title: Wittgenstein's Collection of Nonsense
description: Inspired by Wittengstein’s philosophy of language, Jonathan Rée asks whether any nonsense really is just nonsense, or an attempt to express the impossible

title: Erotic Capital
description: Catherine Hakim celebrates the power of 'erotic capital', the overlooked asset she argues is at the heart of how we succeed in life and relationships

title: Purity and Dirt
description: From antibacterial sprays to obsessive cleaning-up of our deeds, attitudes & language, what is it about dirt that places cleanliness next to godliness?

title: Is the media democratic?
description: Following the Leveson inquiry and the phone hacking scandal the press finds itself beseiged. But what is the best answer for society and our democracy?

title: How to Change the World
description: Brian Eno and James Thornton debate how to change the world through social justice, political economy & environmental law to bring about a new renaissance

title: Are There Really Many Worlds?
description: Quantum theorists claim their science reveals the existence of many worlds. Philosopher of physics James Ladyman on the multiverse theory

title: Europe After the Reign
description: All the signs are that Europe's economic dominance is over, as Asia continues its rise. Will Europe's global cultural influence decline as a consequence?

title: The mind's eye
description: Galen Strawson, Nicholas Humphrey, David Malone debate: For scientists and philosophers the idea of the soul has been out of fashion for 200 years. But can science explain consciousness without it? Or the experience of life?

title: The Schlock of the New
description: Stephen Bayley tells the untold story of the truth about modern art: how giant art corporations became strangely vulnerable to the future

title: Nature's Hidden Persuaders
description: Nicholas Humphrey examines studies on one of medicine's most mysterious phenomena, the placebo effect's role in psychology and human body

title: Hawking vs philosophy
description: Is philosophy dead? Was Stephen Hawking right? Biologist Lewis Wolpert, philosopher Steve Fuller and journalist Jonathan Derbyshire investigate the limits of science and philosophy.Derbyshire investigate the limits of science and philosophy.

title: Empire Strikes Back
description: Momentous decisions are increasingly driven not by national governments but by supranational and regional alliances. Is it the end of governments and nation-states?

title: Economic Democracy
description: Peter Tatchell outlines his vision for a fair, successful and accountable economy: the theory and practice of economic democracy & democratic capitalism

title: Our Hopeless Future & Other Comedy
description: Our Hopeless Future & Other Comedy is a talk by novelist and comics icon Warren Ellis on dystopian America, the space age and the power of Twitter

title: On Humans and Animals
description: Philosophers Peter Singer & Mary Midgley debate the future of bioethics in the light of human and animal rights & our attitudes to other forms of life

title: The Theory of Everything
description: Physicists John Ellis & Frank Close on the limits of knowledge, the quantum theory and the grand final theory of everything, unifying matter and the universe

title: States of Play
description: Award-winning poet Don Paterson, FT columnist Harry Eyres, and author and game designer and philosopher Chris Bateman find themselves at play with play.

title: Psychiatry and the Meaning of Pain
description: Mark Salter defends the value of sadness & depression – against the medicalisation of emotions - in this talk about psychiatry and the meaning of pain

title: Meat, Metal, Code
description: Famed for pushing the boundaries of performance art and biotechnology, Stelarc previews startling new scientific developments set to transform our relationships to our bodies and our selves.

title: Why Marx was right
description: Philosopher and critic Terry Eagleton makes the case for Marx's resurrection, challenging the standard critiques and explaining why the German philosopher's thought remains as relevant as ever.

title: Myths for Modernity
description: Novelist Jim Crace, cultural theorist Nicholas Royle and author Justina Robson examine the importance of reintroducing myths and mythologies in modern times

title: Blinded by the Light
description: Don Cupitt, Simon Armitage and philosophers Angie Hobbs & Barry Smith examine the role of metaphors of light & darkness on reality, knowledge and truth

title: Enhancing Morality
description: Technology will soon have the power to forcibly 'improve' our moral behaviour. Bioethicists Julian Savulescu and John Harris consider what this means for the future of mankind

title: The agony and the ecstasy
description: We take it for granted that eradicating pain is desirable. But is it possible, and do we want, to eliminate agony or ecstasy or is it necessary to human life?

title: Touching Cyberspace
description: Cyberspace is a world without laws or boundaries, and touch-screen technologies have made digital ideas tangible. Nick Harkaway asks where the physicalisation of the net is taking us.

title: The Fantasy of Technology
description: The fantasy of technology questions whether technological innovation viewed as a driver of progress or salvation isn’t clouding more meaningful human goals

title: James Lovelock: Creativity in Science & Gaia Theory
description: James Lovelock on the origins of the Gaia Theory, being a lone scientist and creativity in science. With diplomat and environmentalist Crispin Tickell

title: Reason and The Decline of Violence
description: Steven Pinker's Theory Explored. Steven Pinker makes the case for the historical decline of violence. Roger Bolton, Andrew Copson and Judith Marquand cross-examine.

title: Venus In Furs
description: Venus in Furs is a debate on sadomasochism, BDSM & the limits of sexuality. The role of the Internet in giving desire a new twist, with new ideas & examples

title: The Eureka Moment
description: Scientific advance is a roll call of eureka moments. Does the institutional character of big science research militate against these critical imaginative leaps?

title: The Best of Times?
description: The Best of Times: The Rise of India, modern China & the future of the West questions the impact of rampant consumerism and infinite economic growth

title: Neuroscience and the Mystery of Music
description: Can neuroscience uncover the purpose of art or the philosophy of music? Raymond Tallis explains why our love for music remains beyond science's grasp

title: Diane Abbott: Beyond Downton Abbey
description: Diane Abbott responds to Downton Abbey, presenting a less saccharine, refreshingly outspoken view of British history.

title: Time's arrow
description: What is time? A dimension, a place, a social construct, or something more mysterious? Philosophy meets physics to debate the reality & nature of time

title: Pythagoras' Dream
description: Pythagoras thought the key to universe was Mathematics. But even scientific realism questions the place of maths as the ultimate character of the world

title: The Ultimate Map of Reality
description: 20th Century thought and science seemed to render metaphysics obsolete, but could a revival be on the agenda? Should such talk be left to priests and mystics?
filename: hgtlgi12 -70 - The Ultimate map of reality.mp4

title: After Capitalism
description: Is capitalism the only viable economic system, or can we imagine a post-capitalist society? Debating a future based not on equality, but fairness.

title: The Fifth Crime
description: Should ecocide – man-made environmental destruction - sit alongside genocide as a crime against humanity? Radical ecologist Polly Higgins makes a powerful case

title: The Physical and Psychological Differences Between Men and Women
